value.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for watching for regressions against baselines a person accepted
value.lets_workers: Keep baselines as nouns, from page screenshots by hash to metrics with tolerances, API response shapes and video QA numbers; measure every change again under the same settings; compare by fixed rules and measure every mismatch twice more before reporting it, so a flaky check is told apart from a real regression; record regressions as findings and flaky checks as findings against the check; and leave every new baseline to a person.

The person's decision written as the next baseline set, exactly.
On every change that could move a baseline.
After a release, read-only checks of the live version, compared here as check results.
For a new render, the numbers this pack compares.
The rules, with two reruns of every mismatch.
Findings for regressions and flaky checks; proposals for a person.

complements: Video numbers come from the video QA pack's extended report on the exact bytes; this pack compares them with the last accepted render.

After a release, the release and verify pack's parity check and smoke checks read the live version; this pack keeps their results as check-result baselines, and its workers never switch a live version.
Screenshots are captured with the screenshot design review pack's matrix, and a changed capture is judged by its design rules before a person sees it.
Findings go through the findings to fixes pack; a check that keeps flaking goes to the checks of checks pack.

value.title: How baselines are captured, accepted, measured again and compared
value.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.
lifecycle: capture-baseline measures the accepted version under named settings and writes a candidate baseline set.
accept-baseline is a person's verb: they accept a candidate, or later replace items with new measurements or change a tolerance, and every earlier set is kept.
apply-acceptance writes exactly what the person decided as the next baseline set, and nothing else.
remeasure measures a change under exactly the baseline's settings.
compare-to-baseline applies the comparison rules and measures every mismatch again at least twice before it classifies anything.
report-regressions records each regression as a finding, each flaky check as a finding against the check, and proposes accept-baseline for intended changes, improvements and new items.
review-flaky-checks looks across comparisons for checks that keep flaking and proposes fixing or retiring them.
rules: Compare like with like: the same cell, environment, tool versions and inputs, or the item is not comparable.
Rerun before reporting: a mismatch is a regression only if every rerun repeats it.
A missing measurement is missing, never a match; a check that did not run is not a pass.
Only a person moves a baseline; an improvement is a proposal for them, never an update.
Every regression becomes a finding with reproduce, propose-fix, fix, verify-fix and add-regression-guard; the watch itself is the guard once the fix lands.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.
value.when: On every change that could move a baseline: a merge, a build, a render or a release. After a release, the release and verify pack's smoke checks and parity read the live version; this pack compares their results with the baseline.

value.title: Five kinds of baseline and what each stores
value.category_reason: A reusable description of what each kind of baseline holds.

kinds.stores: The SHA-256 of a full-page capture and of its layout facts, per capture cell.
kinds.measure_with: The screenshot design review pack's capture matrix and layout facts, with animations off and fonts settled.
kinds.volatile: Dates, counters and anything the page says changes; mask them in the capture plan, never after the fact.

kinds.stores: A number with its unit, how it was sampled, a tolerance and which direction is better.
kinds.measure_with: The same tool, version and sample count each time, such as the median of five lab runs.
kinds.volatile: Network and machine load; that is what reruns and tolerances are for.

kinds.stores: Every path in a response with its type, and the enum values seen, never the values themselves.
kinds.measure_with: Read-only requests with synthetic data, against a local build or a test target.
kinds.volatile: Ids, timestamps and ordering of keys; shapes ignore them.

kinds.stores: The video QA pack's measured numbers for one file: loudness, true peak, duration, caption cues, blank and frozen frames.
kinds.measure_with: The video QA pack's measurement rules on the exact delivered bytes.
kinds.volatile: None: the same bytes give the same numbers.

kinds.stores: A deterministic check's pass or fail, such as a smoke check or a design rule.
kinds.volatile: None; a check that changes its result on the same input is flaky.

value.title: Comparing a measurement with its baseline
value.category_reason: A zero-call rule: the same baseline, measurement and reruns always give the same outcomes.

outcomes.match: Within the rule for its kind.
outcomes.regression: Outside the rule in the worse direction, on the first run and on every rerun.
outcomes.flaky: Outside the rule on some runs and within it on others.
outcomes.changed: Outside the rule in a better or neutral direction, or a new item; a person decides whether it becomes the baseline.
outcomes.missing: Not measured this time, with the reason; never a match.

by_kind.screenshot: Equal digests match. A different digest is changed when the new capture passes the screenshot design review's rules, and a regression when a rule fails.
by_kind.metric: relative: within amount times the baseline; absolute: within amount; exact: equal; at_most or at_least: a ceiling or floor. Outside it, the better direction is changed and the worse one a regression; when no direction is better, any move outside the rule is a regression.
by_kind.api_shape: A removed path, a changed type or a removed enum value is a regression; an added path or enum value is changed.
by_kind.video_qa: Each number by its metric rule; a QA check that passed and now fails is a regression.
by_kind.check_result: pass to fail is a regression; fail to pass is changed. Count failures, never passes: a new passing test can hide a new failure in a count of passes.

value.rerun: Every outcome other than match is measured again before it is final; see the flake rules.

value.title: Telling a flaky check from a regression
value.category_reason: A zero-call rule: the same runs always give the same verdict.

reruns.spacing: The first rerun at once, the second after at least a minute, same settings.

verdicts.regression: The first run and every rerun are outside the rule in the worse direction.
verdicts.changed: Every run is outside the rule in a better or neutral direction.
verdicts.flaky: Anything else: at least one run within the rule, or runs that move in different directions.

after: A flaky item becomes a finding of kind issue against the check, fingerprinted issue/<check>/flaky-<item>, with all three runs.
A check that flakes three times in thirty days goes to the checks of checks pack's validate-checks, or its tolerance to a person.

To tell a flaky check from a flaky product, run the check three times on the baseline build: steady there means the change behaves intermittently, and the finding becomes an error against the product.
A flaky item is never reported as a product regression, and never silently dropped.

The two synthetic good comparisons pass; each synthetic bad one fails exactly the one check named in fails.
